solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hollywood star, one better wearing Dior pants

indicators.note: wearing: the shuffled letters are put on around the pair, as clothes go round a body
pants as British slang for rubbish signals the fashion house's letters are messed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A film star, one notch better than the rest, is spotted in Dior trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' turns DIOR into DRIO; 'wearing' has DRIO go round ICAP. 'pants' looks like trousers but is the British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo DiCaprio is an actor famous for films such as Titanic, so he is a star of American cinema.

clue.text: Upright character by Kentish Town is a paragon

parts.note: the letter I is an upright stroke
Deal is a town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A notable figure from Kentish Town, the London district, is held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a district of London, but here the words mean a town in Kent: DEAL, a seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a person or thing regarded as perfect, a model to imitate, just as a paragon is.

clue.text: Turn up pressed cider I'm leaving for Roman?

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive

indicators.note: pressed, as apples are crushed for juice, signals the letters of cider are squashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shows up insisting on cider before departing for Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressed' rearranges CIDER as DERCI. The question mark flags that a Roman would say this when going.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is the Italian goodbye, so it is what a person in Rome says on departing.

clue.text: Mount to gallop further

parts.note: to gallop is to rush along at speed
further means more, in addition

explanation.surface: A horseman is told to get on and ride harder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb for getting on a horse; it is the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore is the South Dakota peak carved with the faces of four American presidents.

clue.text: A dubious appearance is all I fixed with liposuction

indicators.note: fixed suggests something doctored or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that liposuction fixed their entire figure, a doubtful look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges ALLI plus LIPOSUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is something that looks other than it really is, so its appearance cannot be trusted.

clue.text: Service provided in area for climbers

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

explanation.surface: A church service is laid on in a region popular with mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a natural region for mountaineers to explore.

clue.text: Did fool go for a sleigh ride south of large thoroughfare?

indicators.note: south of in a down answer places this piece below the other

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords
to sled is to ride on a sledge or sleigh

explanation.surface: Did an idiot take a sleigh ride below a main road?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did fool' looks like a question about a fool; it is the verb, deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead is to deceive someone, so misled is the past tense, the same as fooled.

clue.text: Runner in unfinished sketch

indicators.note: unfinished means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

explanation.surface: An athlete appears in a comedy sketch that has no ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of SKIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is one of the long narrow strips a skier glides on, a runner like a sledge's.

clue.text: Concerned with clothing because this is counterfeit

parts.note: to be in something is to be wearing it as clothing
since means because
re means concerning, with regard to

explanation.surface: Anxiety about clothes, since this outfit is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere describes feelings that are not genuine but put on, like a fake or false article.

clue.text: Two teachers sent back rubbish

indicators.note: sent back means the two teachers' letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: SIR is how a schoolboy addresses a male teacher and BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree held by a teacher

explanation.surface: A pair of teachers return work that is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns SIR BED around to give DEB RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or remains, which is a kind of rubbish.

clue.text: Try drinking wine — it's most pleasing

indicators.note: drinking means the word for try takes the wine into itself

parts.note: to try something is to test it
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to sample a wine because it is the nicest one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastiest is the superlative of tasty, meaning having the most delicious or agreeable flavour.

clue.text: Small ladies, perhaps one from Russia?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
the ladies is British slang for a women's toilet, an example of a lav or lavatory

explanation.surface: Diminutive women, maybe, come from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' looks like people but is the British word for a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Russians are a Slavic people, so a Russian is one example of a Slav, hence the question mark.

clue.text: What's taken when teasing European? It'll knock you out

parts.note: taking the mickey is a British phrase for teasing someone
a Finn is a European from Finland

explanation.surface: Something is swallowed during a teasing session, and it will leave you unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the mickey' (mocking someone) is the British idiom behind the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mickey Finn is a drink secretly spiked with a drug to make the drinker unconscious.

clue.text: Banger, a beauty, introduced by car racing engineers

indicators.note: introduced by means the following piece is preceded by the earlier pieces

parts.note: Formula One motor racing is F1, written FI in crosswords
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cracker is British slang for an attractive person or something excellent

explanation.surface: An old car, a beauty, is brought in by racing engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' looks like an old car; here it is a firework, its British sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a loud firework, and a firecracker is an explosive one of that type.

clue.text: Empty receptacle laid up, moving a number for delivery

indicators.note: moving signals that the outer letters together with laid up are shuffled around
an empty word keeps only its outer letters, its contents removed

explanation.surface: An empty container, laid up for repair, shifts a number for delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves RE from receptacle; 'moving' rearranges RE plus LAIDUP. 'number' is a thing that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidural is an anaesthetic injection into the spine often given in childbirth, a numbing agent used during labour.

clue.text: Maybe Chinese character and ancient Briton love to put on weight

indicators.note: to put on means the weight is added after the other pieces

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton in love starts to gain weight, as might someone Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese writing includes signs that are pictures of what they mean, so its symbols can be picture-signs.

clue.text: Bank at liberty to delay opening

indicators.note: delaying the opening means the first letter is moved later in the word

parts.note: someone at liberty is free

explanation.surface: A bank is free to postpone opening its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to delay opening' moves the F of FREE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the surface of the sea, a bank in the nautical sense.

clue.text: I could be one of these spreading mean slur

definitions.text: I could be one of these

indicators.note: spreading a rumour scatters it about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker admits they might be guilty of spreading a nasty slur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter I is the Roman numeral for one, so it is one of the symbols used for counting.

clue.text: Almost put the wind up Mark

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to put the wind up someone is British slang for to scare them

explanation.surface: Someone nearly frightened a man called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting trace left on skin by a healed wound, a kind of mark.

clue.text: American ate sandwiches and got going

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word for ate holds the abbreviation between its letters

parts.note: to have lunched is to have eaten a midday meal

explanation.surface: An American ate some sandwiches and then set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the verb: LUNCHED encloses A.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch is to set something in motion, so launched means started or set going.

clue.text: Lackey running behind car

indicators.note: behind means this piece comes after the car

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A servant runs along behind the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a servile follower or underling, someone who does menial work like a lackey.

clue.text: Charlie and I, overwhelmed by loneliness, showing concern

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the pair is swallowed up within the word for loneliness

parts.note: solitude is the state of being alone
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie and the speaker, swamped by isolation, show care for each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care for someone's welfare, a synonym of concern.

clue.text: Join large gathering to depose leader

indicators.note: deposing the leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: People are urged to attend a mass meeting aimed at toppling the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to depose leader' drops the R of RALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to unite or combine with another for a shared purpose, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Bedsheets etc from the 14th row

parts.note: a line is a row
N is the fourteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Bed linen comes from the fourteenth row of a shop or warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 14th' means the fourteenth letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is the collective word for household textiles like sheets and pillowcases, named after the fabric.

clue.text: Tennis player, one framing suitable wall decoration

indicators.note: framing means the two outer pieces sit on either side of the word for suitable, like a picture frame

parts.note: Steffi Graf is a German tennis champion
one is the Roman numeral I
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: A tennis star, one framing a fitting decoration for a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' has GRAF and I on either side of FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is writing or drawings sprayed or scratched on walls, an unofficial kind of mural.

clue.text: Flipped over image file showing fruit

indicators.note: flipped over means the letters of the file type are turned to run the other way

parts.note: a GIF is a common computer image file format

explanation.surface: An image file turned upside down shows a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipped over' turns GIF into its reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fig is the soft sweet pear-shaped fruit of the fig tree.

clue.text: Pursuing enquiries in a royal capacity

definitions.meaning: split as ..., acting as a king means in a royal capacity

explanation.surface: Someone is making enquiries while acting as a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words, AS KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is putting questions to people, the same thing as making enquiries.

clue.text: This person's with old dope, a daughter of Will's

parts.note: this person's means the speaker is, I'm
dope and gen are both slang for information

explanation.surface: The speaker is with some old drugs, says a daughter of someone called Will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is William Shakespeare; 'dope' is information, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is the daughter of King Cymbeline in Shakespeare's play Cymbeline, so one of the playwright's characters.

clue.text: At first, nuncio foolishly ignores feature of bull

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is taken
foolishly signals the letters of ignores are rearranged in a silly way

explanation.surface: From the outset, a papal envoy carelessly overlooks something about a papal bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges IGNORES to OSERING. 'bull' looks like a papal decree, as the nuncio suggests, but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring through the nose is traditionally fitted to a bull to lead and control it.
